content_reasoning: currentLiquidationFactorBIPS sets the vault share to zero when the vault collateral is invalid and the pool collateral is valid, so the pool pays the whole liquidation (lines 37-39). This is the rule the finding links to and builds its argument on. The cap that limits the agent's share of the pool payment is in LiquidationFacet.sol, so the second half of the argument cannot be checked here.
patterns_found: vault share set to zero when the vault collateral is invalid, so the pool pays everything

vulnerability_type: liquidation payment rule removes the incentive to replace invalid collateral

content_reasoning: validatePrice adds tradePrice times elapsedTime to cumulativePriceLast, then subtracts cumulativePriceLast and divides by elapsedTime again, so the TWAP always equals the current spot price. The slippage check therefore compares the spot price with itself, as the finding says.
patterns_found: TWAP built from the current spot price, so it always equals the spot price
slippage check that compares the spot price with itself
issues: buyBack and convertToV3 are callers in other contracts; the broken calculation itself is in this file.
vulnerability_type: TWAP calculation collapses to the spot price

content_reasoning: updatePrice adds snapshot.averagePrice times elapsedTime to snapshot.cumulativePrice and then estimates total time as cumulativePrice divided by averagePrice, which is exactly the code quoted in the finding. The new average is then used for the slippage check and stored.
patterns_found: cumulative price accumulates the previous average instead of the observed price
total time estimated by dividing cumulativePrice by averagePrice
issues: `lastPrice` does not occur in the code; it is the finding's name for the observed price the formula should use.
vulnerability_type: incorrect TWAP formula in oracle update

content_reasoning: registerAgentsWithSignature builds the message hash from operator, service owner, service ID, agent instances, agent IDs and nonce, and it has no deadline parameter or expiry check. After the signature check it calls registerAgentsTokenDeposit with the operator address, as the finding describes.
patterns_found: operator signature with no deadline or expiry check
bond deposit taken for the operator address after the signature check
issues: The hash itself is built in OperatorSignedHashes.sol and the safeTransferFrom from the operator is in ServiceRegistryTokenUtility; this file shows the call without a deadline.
vulnerability_type: signature without deadline can be reused later

content_reasoning: _withdraw copies balance into updatedBalance, calls the virtual _transfer for each receiver, and writes balance back only after the loop. _claim and _unstake reach this path and the file has no reentrancy guard, so the first issue in the finding can be seen here.
patterns_found: storage balance written after external transfers
no reentrancy guard on claim and unstake
issues: The second issue in the finding, about ServiceManager.create and onERC721Received, is in ServiceManager.sol and is not in this file.
The third problem_code block (lines 85-208) comes from the ServiceManager.sol link and shows unrelated interface and error code.
vulnerability_type: reentrancy in reward withdrawal, balance written after transfers

content_reasoning: validatePrice reads blockTimestampLast from getReserves and returns false when it equals block.timestamp, which is the check at lines 68-72. Calling sync() on the pair earlier in the same block sets blockTimestampLast to the current time, so the victim's check fails.
patterns_found: price check returns false when the pair was updated in the same block
issues: sync() is a function of the Uniswap V2 pair, not of this file.
vulnerability_type: front-run sync() makes the oracle price check fail

content_reasoning: validatePrice is a view function that extends the stored snapshot.averagePrice over elapsedTime and never refreshes the snapshot or limits its age. This is the stale TWAP calculation the finding quotes.
patterns_found: TWAP extrapolated from the last stored average with no limit on its age
issues: BuyBackBurner and LiquidityManagerOptimism are callers in other contracts.
vulnerability_type: stale TWAP used for price validation

content_reasoning: checkpoint adds the next epoch's maxBond to effectiveBond in advance (lines 1279-1280) and later corrects effectiveBond only when the actual maxBond is larger than the predicted one, with no branch for the smaller case. This is the one-way correction the finding describes.
patterns_found: effectiveBond corrected only upward
next epoch maxBond credited to effectiveBond in advance
issues: Lines 1248-1267 already mix the old and new inflation rates when the next epoch is predicted to cross a year boundary. The finding does not discuss this, so the size of the over-credit could not be confirmed from the code.
The second problem_code block (lines 67-179) comes from the TokenomicsConstants.sol link and shows unrelated error declarations.
vulnerability_type: bond credit not reduced when actual inflation is lower than predicted

content_reasoning: updatePrice weighs the new price against the historical weight, cumulativePrice divided by averagePrice, and returns false without changing averagePrice or lastUpdated when the price is outside maxSlippage. Once the market price moves past the limit, later updates keep failing and validatePrice keeps using the old average.
patterns_found: update rejected without changing the stored average when the price moves beyond maxSlippage
historical weight in the average keeps growing
issues: The finding says cumulativePrice stays frozen, but the code writes the increase to storage before the slippage check returns false. This does not remove the deadlock.
vulnerability_type: oracle update blocked after the price moves beyond the slippage limit

content_reasoning: suppliedBalance decodes four uint64 values from the 0x811 precompile and keeps only the fourth one, the supplied amount, which is the line the finding marks as the bug. suppliedUsdcEvm and suppliedNotionalUsdcFromPerp build on this value, so the borrow side is lost before the backing is summed.
patterns_found: precompile response decoded for the supply value only, borrow fields discarded
issues: The backing sum that adds the supplied value without subtracting borrow debt (_readL1Backing, totalBackingSigned, surplus) is in MonetrixAccountant.sol, and settle is in MonetrixVault.sol. Only the reader part of the bug is in this file.
vulnerability_type: borrow debt left out of the backing calculation

content_reasoning: The checkEpoch modifier only requires that block.timestamp has reached nextEpochPoint and then adds one to epoch, and nextEpochPoint is startTime plus epoch times PERIOD. After a long pause, allocateSeigniorage can be called once for every missed hour, as the finding says.
patterns_found: epoch advanced by one per call instead of computed from elapsed time
issues: The reward claim through Staking.sol mentioned in the impact is in another file.
vulnerability_type: epoch counter catches up one step per call after a pause

content_reasoning: _zapToken calls _refundDust after adding liquidity, but addLiquidity, addLiquidityETH and executeOperation call the router and never call _refundDust. Tokens the router does not use stay in the Zapper, as the finding says.

issues: problem_code was empty because the link has no line numbers; the whole file was checked.

reward calculation controlled by unchecked parameters

content_reasoning: getUnderlyingSupply prices aHYPE from the contract balance plus the DelegatorSummary and spot balance precompiles, and withdraw uses it to fix the withdrawal price. processQueues sends HYPE to HyperCore, and the precompile values only change in the next block, so a withdraw in the same block uses a wrong price.
patterns_found: precompile balances read in the same block after funds are sent to HyperCore
withdrawal price fixed from stale balances
vulnerability_type: stale precompile balances in the same block give a wrong withdrawal price

content_reasoning: _createVestingStreams loops over every address in contributors and calls sablierV2.createWithDurationsLL once per address, and depositEth adds new contributors with no upper limit. Many small contributions can push this loop past the block gas limit.
